name: Country Furniture Warehouse
old_description: and you will see why we have been successfully serving the Crofton community for over 25 years.  Family owned, we specialize in selling quality wood furniture for every room in your home.  So stop by and check us out and you'll se why we are Crofton's best-kept secret.Crofton Furniture Warehouse is located at:
about:
Country Furniture Warehouse, operating as Crofton Furniture Warehouse, has been a fixture on Defense Highway in Gambrills, Maryland for over 25 years. The family-owned retailer occupies a showroom where it has served the Crofton community since its founding, though the exact year is not publicly stated.

The business specializes in selling solid-wood furniture for every room in the house, with a particular emphasis on Amish-crafted pieces. Its inventory spans kitchen, dining, bedroom, and living room collections, all sourced directly from Amish workshops rather than produced in-house. The showroom operates Tuesday through Saturday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., with most Sundays open from 12 p.m. to 4 p.m., and remains closed on Mondays.

The customer base is almost entirely residential, drawing shoppers from Crofton and neighboring areas in Anne Arundel County. The company does not advertise commercial, hospitality, or contract furnishings accounts, and its marketing focuses on local foot traffic and word-of-mouth referrals.

What sets the operation apart, according to its own description, is the combination of family ownership and a direct supply line to Amish builders, which it promotes as offering quality wood furniture without intermediary markups. The website, built on the Homestead platform, reinforces this local, direct-to-consumer positioning.

name: Country Hillside Designs LLC.
old_description: since 2010 and I enjoy every customer I have. I have at my disposal,  a vinyl cutter, A digital print and cut printer, 2 heat presses and 2 commercial embroidery machines. In 2021 we changed the name to Country Hillside Designs.
about:
Country Hillside Designs operates from Ryder, North Dakota, where owner Patti Shelkey founded the business in 2010. The company adopted its current name in 2021, evolving from Shelkey's vision of a cottage-style shop where customers could explore rooms filled with designed apparel. Shelkey, who grew up around horses, cattle, and the outdoors, built the business around storytelling through stitching and printing.

The shop runs two commercial embroidery machines, a digital print-and-cut printer, a vinyl cutter, and two heat presses. A small team of designers and technicians works with clients to develop custom artwork, then produces embroidered and printed apparel — jackets, vests, blankets, towels, quilts, bags, and spirit wear — using materials sourced from apparel suppliers. Screen printing is also offered for larger event runs.

Customers range from local businesses needing corporate jackets and ranch logos to schools and youth organizations ordering 4-H towels and graduation blankets. The company also serves rodeo circuits, family reunions, sports teams, and the western-wear market, selling directly at events such as the Badlands Circuit Finals Rodeo. Gift shoppers and individual buyers round out the client base.

Shelkey frames the work as narrative: each embroidered logo or printed design marks a family story, a milestone, or a brand identity. The company emphasizes personalized service, quality-first production, and hands-on expert care as its guiding principles.

about:
Cove Stake & Wood Products Inc has operated from Martinsburg, Pennsylvania since 1987. The company was established as a family-owned and operated business and continues under that ownership today, serving customers across the United States from its Curryville Road location.

The company manufactures and wholesales a range of wooden products including stakes, slats, lath, rough-cut lumber, pallets, and crates. A two-step quality process is used to reduce rejects and breakage, aiming to lower total costs for buyers. Production volumes, facility size, and employee headcount are not publicly disclosed.

Customers span residential, commercial, and construction sectors, with specific mention of surveying jobs that use stakes and lath. The firm also supplies pallets and crates for material handling and shipping needs across those same markets.

The business emphasizes competitive pricing, on-time delivery, and free estimates as part of its value proposition. Its longevity and family ownership are presented as indicators of reliability, while the quality-control process is cited as a differentiator that reduces waste and cost for end users.

name: Cox Woodworking
old_description: Cox Woodworking was founded in 1981 by master cabinetmaker Terry Cox. He is still hanging around; designing, drafting, talking with clients, and working in the shop. Over the years we have grown into a 4500 square foot shop with several highly skilled cabinetmakers and the resources to build any project our clients can imagine.
about:
Cox Woodworking operates from Westmoreland, New Hampshire. The company was founded in 1981 by master cabinetmaker Terry Cox, who remains actively involved in design, drafting, client consultation, and shop work. What began as a one-person cabinetmaking operation has grown into a 4,500-square-foot facility staffed by several skilled cabinetmakers.

The shop produces custom cabinets and architectural millwork, fabricating windows, doors, custom moldings, gates, pillars, curved work, and turnings. It also delivers whole-house residential packages that encompass luxury kitchens, baths, libraries, wine cellars, home offices, and entertainment centers. Projects move from in-house design and drafting through fabrication in the 4,500-square-foot shop.

The firm serves high-end residential clients and architectural projects across New York, New England, and beyond. Its work has been featured in publications including New York Times Magazine, Boston Home Magazine, Antiques Magazine, and House & Garden.

The company emphasizes a commitment to long-term customer satisfaction and a willingness to tackle challenging projects, with the founder’s hands-on involvement ensuring quality at every stage.

name: Crabtree Auto
old_description: Welcome to Crabtree Auto. We are your premier shop for new & used car parts, auto salvage, & used car part sales. Our company has over 70 years of experience in the auto salvage industry and has served individuals and commercial clients all across Utah. Crabtree Auto buys damaged vehicles that are 10 years old and newer, and we sell the undamaged parts to body shops, individuals and more.
about:
Crabtree Auto operates from Riverdale, Utah, just outside Ogden. The business traces its roots to a post-World War II body shop in Logan, where the Crabtree brothers began selling parts from their own vehicles. That parts operation evolved into a full-scale salvage yard, and in 1947 the company relocated to its current Riverdale location. Dahl Crabtree became sole owner and later passed the business to his sons, Miles and Colin Crabtree, who modernized the facilities. Today the third generation of the family directs the company.

The yard purchases damaged vehicles ten model years old or newer, then dismantles, cleans, and tests the usable components. Inventory includes transmissions, engines, body panels (bumpers, fenders, hoods, doors), lighting, glass, mirrors, interior parts, tires, wheels, drivetrain and brake components. Thousands of cars and light trucks are pre-dismantled and shelved for immediate pickup or delivery. The facility serves both walk-in customers and commercial accounts across northern Utah.

Primary customers are collision repair shops, insurance companies, other salvage yards, and individual vehicle owners. The company also works with commercial fleets and local repair businesses throughout Utah.

Crabtree Auto distinguishes itself through its ARA Certified Auto Recycler status and membership in the United Recyclers Group, which requires adherence to quality standards for recycled parts. The operation’s long-standing slogan — “CLEAN - ORGANIZED - QUICK SERVICE” — reflects its focus on facility upkeep and fast turnaround.

Crazy Wood Works emphasizes clear timelines, transparent pricing, and dependable service from start to finish. The business positions its locally made, craftsmanship-driven approach as a differentiator, offering personalized service for each project.

name: Creation Audio Labs
old_description: a manufacturer of studio quality pro-audio electronics, electric guitar and bass effect pedals.
about:
Creation Audio Labs operates from Lebanon, Tennessee, where it was founded in 1996. The company builds studio-quality professional audio electronics, electric guitar and bass effect pedals, and also restores vintage audio equipment.

Its product line includes the MW1 studio tool, Redeemer onboard buffer, Holy Fire overdrive/distortion, MK.4.23 clean boost, Funkulator slap bass pedal, and the Grizzly Bass overdrive/distortion pedal. Beyond manufacturing, the shop provides custom recording console modifications, upgrades, and repair services for professional audio sound boards, with specific expertise in TL Audio, Trident A-Range, and Crown Audio amplifier repairs.

The company serves musicians, recording studios, and audio engineers worldwide, and cooperates with partner shops in selected countries. Notable users include Peter Frampton, who employs the MK.4.23 clean boost, and Ricky Skaggs, who uses the Grizzly Bass pedal.

Creation Audio Labs emphasizes hands-on restoration of vintage gear and custom console work, drawing on decades of experience in hum elimination and analog circuit design. The founder notes 30 years of practical studio troubleshooting, which informs the design of their pedals and studio tools.

name: Creation Technologies
old_description: Creation delivers maximum efficiency and optimum product quality end-to-end.
about:
Creation Technologies is headquartered in Westminster, Colorado, and was founded in 1991 on the principle that electronics manufacturing should be a collaborative partnership rather than a transactional exchange. The company has grown from that founding belief into a global electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider with 13 manufacturing locations across the United States, Canada, Mexico, and China.

The company delivers end-to-end electronics manufacturing, spanning design engineering, new product introduction (NPI), printed circuit board assembly, box build, system integration, interconnect solutions, sheet metal fabrication, conformal coating, and aftermarket repair and refurbishment. Its global team of over 3,000 professionals supports low- to mid-volume production for complex, regulated programs, with dedicated rapid prototyping and value-engineering centers in Denver and other sites.

Creation serves three core markets: aerospace and defense, medical and life sciences, and tech industrial. Its customer base includes OEMs building mission-critical systems such as defense communications and emergency response equipment, dental diagnostic devices, hard-disk-drive tracking systems, automatic test equipment, and vehicle data solutions. The company holds ITAR registration, FDA registration, and Canadian Controlled Goods certification to meet the security and regulatory demands of these sectors.

Creation differentiates itself with a 'Thinking in Action' continuous-improvement methodology that has helped customers cut inventory carrying costs by up to 65%, halve field failure rates, and raise on-time shipment performance from 80% to 98.4%. The firm emphasizes lean production programs, proactive supply chain risk mitigation, and a culture described as 'big enough to scale, small enough to care.'

name: Creations Foods US Inc.
old_description: Our in-house innovation team works with partners and specializes in gluten-free recipe development to make some of the tastiest cookies and crackers on the planet.
about:
Creations Foods US Inc. operates a state-of-the-art baking facility in Ferndale, Washington, positioned in the Pacific Northwest with access to major shipping routes across the U.S. and Canada. The company runs an SQF-certified, gluten-free plant designed for industrial-scale production of baked snacks.

The facility houses specialized high-volume inline ovens that produce extruded baked goods and sandwich cookies. An in-house innovation team develops gluten-free recipes for cookies, crackers, cheese crisps, and granola. Creations Foods manufactures its own branded lines — including Moon Cheese, Highkey Snacks, AwYeah, and REAL COOKIES — while also providing private-label and co-manufacturing services for partner brands. Finished goods are packed in stand-up pouches for retail distribution.

The company serves retailers and national brands seeking gluten-free snack production. Its customer base includes brands that market products such as Moon Cheese crunchy cheese snacks, Highkey low-sugar protein snacks, AwYeah mini cookies, and REAL COOKIES healthy cookies. Creations Foods emphasizes a commercialization process that moves concepts from development through to high-volume output.

Creations Foods states that its operation is built on core values of health commitment, humility, agility, and collaboration. The company says it was founded on the belief that eating better should be an easy choice, and it differentiates itself through its gluten-free recipe expertise, SQF-certified food safety standards, and scalable oven technology.

name: Creative Devices, Inc.
old_description: Specializing since 1970 in Microscopy, Probe Stations, Semiconductor Test and Semiconductor Materials Analysis
about:
Creative Devices, Inc. is based in Middletown, Delaware. The company traces its roots to 1970 when it was established as Micron Optics, Inc., serving as the Nikon microscope dealer for New Jersey. In 1990, the owners sold the Micron Optics name and transferred the Nikon franchise to Sylvax Scientific, then continued operations under the Creative Devices, Inc. name, shifting focus to semiconductor inspection, test, and materials research.

The company manufactures a range of equipment for semiconductor testing and analysis, including semiconductor probe stations, custom optics and optical systems, infrared inspection systems, Raman spectroscopy microscopes, and emission microscopes. It also designs custom probe stations for high- and low-voltage applications and other unique requirements. In addition to manufacturing, Creative Devices acts as a distributor for microscope optics and related equipment from suppliers such as Mitutoyo, Motic, Prior Scientific, New Wave Research, Meiji, and Princeton Instruments. The firm also offers consulting services for microscope and probe station design, laser trimming, Raman spectroscopy, high-voltage testing, and emissions microscopy.

Creative Devices serves the semiconductor industry, providing probe station and microscopy solutions for inspection, testing, and materials research. Its customers include semiconductor manufacturers and research organizations that require custom optical systems, probe stations, and spectroscopy equipment for applications such as laser trimming, high-voltage testing, and emissions microscopy.

The company emphasizes its decades of experience in probe station and microscope design, offering consulting and custom fabrication to address unique application challenges.
